text.p: The Interval Coverage Graph displays the percentage of time covered by a certain interval set, e.g. a state or a custom interval. For example, when tracing a state machine, this can show the amount of time spent in a certain state.

The example below shows a state machine in two ways. Above is the Trace View view showing the state transitions over time (using horizontal mode) and below is the Interval Coverage Graph. This makes it easier to see anomalies in state machine behavior and other interval durations. The Interval Plot may also be used for similar purposes, but shows the absolute duration for each occurrence.

ul.li: For a state machine, this view will show the amount of time spent in each state. In this case, the total should always be 100%.
If used with the Actor Fragments/(All) interval set, this will display CPU load across all cores. In this case, the total will add up to (number of cores) * 100%.
If used with the Actor Instances/(All) interval set, this will show some form of demand for processing time.

text.p: By default, the displayed view port is divided into 50 time slices. The number of slices can be changed via the Resolution or Time Resolution menus.
Note that interval coverage may exceed 100% for interval sets containing overlapping intervals, e.g. when used for tracking queue messages.
